senses.definition: Very broad; pertaining or appropriate to large classes or groups as opposed to specific instances.
examples: Capri pants can be a generic term for any cropped slim pants.

quotes.text: […] the essence is that such self-describing poets describe what is in them, but not peculiar to them, – what is generic, not what is special and individual.
quotes.reference: 1864, Walter Bagehot, “Wordsworth, Tennyson, and Browning; or, Pure, Ornate, and Grotesque Art in English Poetry”, in The National Review, volume 19:

senses.definition: Lacking in precision, often in an evasive fashion; vague; imprecise.
(pharmacology) Of a product or drug, not having a brand name; nonproprietary in design or contents; fungible with the rest of its class.

quotes.text: The four-and-one-half-day trial was centered on acts that neither she nor prosecutors dispute: On July 13, 2012, she drove her Lexus S.U.V. erratically after swallowing Zolpidem, a generic form of the sleep medication Ambien.
quotes.reference: 2014 February 28, Joseph Berger, “Fast Acquittal for Kennedy, Whose Name Put Prosecutors in Bind”, in The New York Times, →ISSN, archived from the original on 28 Aug 2022:

senses.definition: (taxonomy) Pertaining to genera of life instead of particular species thereof.
examples: There are scores of generic names within the order Decapoda, which includes many sea creatures that are called shrimp.

senses.definition: (grammar, nonstandard) Specifying neither masculine nor feminine; epicene; unisex.
examples: Words like salesperson and firefighter are generic.
This included criticism of the generic use of man to include men and women.

senses.definition: (computing) Of a procedure, written so as to operate on any data type, the type required being passed as a parameter.
(geometry) Of a point, having coordinates that are algebraically independent over the base field.

quotes.text: Both [films] test formal and generic boundaries.

examples: That movie was so generic; it was such a bore!

senses.definition: A product sold under a generic name.
A wine that is a combination of several wines, or made from a combination of several grape varieties.
(grammar) A term that specifies neither male nor female.

quotes.text: […]a male-centered perspective[…]has resulted in false generics in everyday life[…]
quotes.reference: 1998, Jacqueline A. Dienemann, Nursing administration: managing patient care:

senses.definition: (toponymy) The part of a toponym that identifies the feature's type.

quotes.text: Where the generic of an English-language place name has been translated into French, it is essential to restore it to its original English form when translating the French document into English.
quotes.reference: 2024 July 29, “geographical names: translation”, in Writing Tips Plus, Ottawa: Translation Bureau, retrieved 09 Nov 2024:
